account:
Today is day one, and I have arrived at the mill for my ten o'clock grain inspection. I reviewed the appointment books this morning; later I have council letters, three o'clock tea with the neighbour, and an eighteen-hundred great-hall lighting inspection with the builder. The builder says eight lanterns are installed. That is confirmed town business, not evidence of bridge or port works.

The unusual issue is the talk about grain supplies. The secretary reports overhearing the builder discuss a grain shortage, seek the miller's assistance, and mention forty-six hay bales. I have not verified that number or what it represents. The neighbour says she saw the baker give bread to the innkeeper yesterday, heard the innkeeper ask about spare wheat or hay, and heard freight say they were seeking the miller about arrangements. She called at the mill this morning but got no answer. She also reports that the baker said yesterday's bread arrangements went smoothly and that fresh bread is being baked today. Taken together, this may concern coordinating grain and bread supplies, but I do not yet know whether there is an actual shortage, who needs supplies, or what agreements exist.

There is also vague talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' repeated by townsfolk near the mill just now. Yesterday both the secretary and builder denied having any confirmed bridge or port proposal; the builder said his business was the hall lighting. The repeated phrase contains no concrete details, so I regard it as an unverified rumour rather than a project. I have asked a nearby townsman whether the miller is here. My next purpose is to locate the miller, inspect the grain, and clarify the supply reports firsthand.
